dc.description.abstract.value:
Summary of the Territorial Waters, Continental Shelf, Exclusive Economic Zone and Other Maritime Zones Act, 1976
Objective
The Territorial Waters, Continental Shelf, Exclusive Economic Zone and Other Maritime Zones Act, 1976 was enacted to define India's maritime zones and regulate the exercise of sovereignty, sovereign rights, jurisdiction, and control over its territorial waters, contiguous zone, continental shelf, exclusive economic zone (EEZ), and other maritime areas. The Act provides the legal framework for protecting India's maritime interests, managing marine resources, and safeguarding national security. 
Key Provisions
•	Territorial Waters: Declares India's sovereignty over its territorial waters, extending up to 12 nautical miles from the baseline, along with the airspace above, seabed, and subsoil. 
•	Contiguous Zone: Empowers the Central Government to declare a contiguous zone extending up to 24 nautical miles from the baseline, where India may enforce customs, fiscal, immigration, and sanitary laws. 
•	Continental Shelf: Confers sovereign rights on India over its continental shelf for exploring and exploiting mineral and other natural resources of the seabed and subsoil. 
•	Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ): Provides for the declaration of an Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ) extending up to 200 nautical miles from the baseline, where India has sovereign rights over the exploration, exploitation, conservation, and management of natural resources. 
•	Maritime Boundaries: Empowers the Central Government to determine maritime boundaries with neighbouring coastal States through agreements or other lawful means. 
•	Regulation of Foreign Activities: Authorises the Central Government to regulate scientific research, resource exploitation, installation of offshore structures, and the entry and passage of foreign vessels in designated maritime areas. 
•	Rule-making Power: Empowers the Central Government to make rules and issue notifications for implementing and administering the provisions of the Act.

dc.description.abstract.value:
Summary of Oudh Estates Act 1869

Purpose
•	Define the rights of Taluqdárs and others in certain estates in Oudh.
•	Regulate the succession to these estates.

Key Definitions (from Section 2 - Interpretation-clause)
•	Transfer: Alienation inter vivos.
•	Will: Legal declaration of intentions regarding property.
•	Codicil: Supplement to a Will.
•	Signed/Registered: Specific to affixing a mark and registration under Oudh's rules.
•	Minor/Minority: Person under 18 years of age.
•	Taluqdár: Person listed in the first of the lists mentioned in Section 8.
•	Grantee: Person with proprietary right conferred by the British Government.
•	Estate: Taluqa or immovable property held by a Taluqdár or Grantee.
•	Heir/Legatee: Heir under the Act (excluding widows under special provisions) / Person bequeathed property.

Provisions (Limited to Provided Context)
1.	Short Title & Extent: Cited as "The Oudh Estates' Act, 1869", applying only to specified estates.
2.	Interpretation Clause: Defines key terms as above.

dc.identifier.preamble_description.value:
THE OUDH ESTATES ACT, 1869
ACT NO. 1 OF 1869.
PASSED BY THE GOVERNOR GENERAL OF INDIA IN COUNCIL.
(Received the assent of the Governor General on the 12th January 1869).
An Act to define the rights of Taluqdárs and others in certain estates in Oudh, and to regulate the succession thereto.
Preamble.---WHEREAS, after the re-occupation of Oudh by the British Government in the year 1858, the proprietary right in divers estates in that province was, under certain conditions, conferred by the British Government upon certain Taluqdars and others ; and whereas doubts may arise as to the nature of the rights of the said Taluqdars and others in such estates, and as to the course of succession thereto ; and whereas it is expedient to prevent such doubts, and to regulate such course, and to provide for such other matters connected therewith as are hereinafter mentioned ; It is hereby enacted as follows :----
